mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in a month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2% year-over-year, the combination signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in a month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Housing Starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 1% quarter-over-quarter and the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, the combination signals a potential economic slowdown with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: economic slowdown with tightening monetary policy
failure_condition: If GDPC1 QoQ growth < 1% and FEDFUNDS > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
